readmeSections.heading: Agent Linux
readmeSections.body:
**Give your agent a Linux computer.**

Run a persistent Debian/Xfce desktop on your Apple silicon Mac. Connect an agent over MCP, watch it work, and take over the same desktop when you need to. The guest comes with Chromium, Firefox ESR, a file manager, a terminal and a text editor.

[Quick start](#quick-start) · [Control the desktop](#control-the-desktop) · [Manage workspaces](#manage-workspaces) · [Compatibility](#compatibility-and-limits) · [Documentation](#documentation)

![Illustration of an Agent Linux workspace showing a browser and terminal in a Debian/Xfce desktop on an Apple silicon Mac.](docs/assets/readme-workspace.svg)

*Illustration featuring the [offline project-budget demo](docs/demo.md).*

[Supervised guest agent runs](docs/agent-runs.md) provide bounded Codex/Claude/custom
runner supervision and an experimental Grok adapter. Real ARM64 guest agent runs
are not yet qualified; hosted agents such as Devin are not claimed to run in the VM.

> **Available today: source-built local developer preview.** Tested on one M4 Pro Mac. No public binaries or VM images are published, and the native app is not notarized. Cloud and billing are development prototypes, not a hosted or paid service. See [launch readiness](docs/launch-readiness.md).

readmeSections.heading: Quick start
readmeSections.body:
On an Apple-silicon Mac, paste this into a terminal:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ADITYADEV4145/AgentLinux/main/install.sh | bash
```

This **builds from source locally**, installs the CLI without sudo, builds an
optional unsigned (ad-hoc signed, not notarized) Mac app, and launches Linux.
If prompted to install Xcode Command Line Tools, finish that installation and
re-run the same command. Python 3.9+ from the tools is sufficient. It downloads
source, Go 1.26.9 if needed, Go modules, and pinned Lima unless a supported Lima
is on PATH. First launch downloads the Debian image and guest packages.
Re-run to upgrade; it never edits shell profiles or Gatekeeper settings.
See [installer options and uninstall](docs/release.md#one-command-source-install).

For guided project import, fresh guest agent authentication and a task/verification
record, run `agent-linux onboard --project /absolute/path/to/project`.
See [first-run onboarding](docs/onboarding.md) for safety boundaries and limits.
Bare `agent-linux` in a terminal still starts/resumes Linux and opens its viewer.

readmeSections.heading: 1. Build and check your Mac
readmeSections.body:
- **Host:** Apple silicon Mac with hardware virtualization; see the [tested configuration](#compatibility-and-limits).
- **Tools (manual build):** Git, macOS developer command-line tools, OpenSSH, [Go 1.26.9](https://go.dev/dl/), Python 3.9+, and [Lima 2.2.1 or stable 2.3.x](https://github.com/lima-vm/lima/releases). If you use Homebrew, run `brew install lima` and confirm the version with `limactl --version`. The build may fetch the pinned Go toolchain if it is missing.
- **Storage and network:** Have at least 30 GiB free for the default VM (2 CPUs, 4 GiB RAM, 24 GiB logical disk). First startup needs internet access for the pinned Debian image (~322 MiB) and guest packages.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/ADITYADEV4145/AgentLinux.git
cd AgentLinux
make build
./bin/agent-linux doctor --json
```

The examples assume a supported `limactl` is on your PATH. Otherwise add `--lima /absolute/path/to/limactl` to each local command, before any positional arguments. For a reproducible build, verifying a downloaded archive, an optional private install without sudo, upgrades or uninstall, see [packaging and release](docs/release.md).

readmeSections.heading: 2. Start Linux and watch in your browser
readmeSections.body:
In terminal A:

```sh
./bin/agent-linux start --viewer web --view-only
```

Open the private loopback URL the CLI prints. Leave this command running while you connect your agent. This starts or resumes a local VM, waits for its desktop, and leaves human input disabled so the agent can act. It does not create cloud resources.

readmeSections.heading: 3. Connect an agent
readmeSections.body:
In terminal B:

```sh
./bin/agent-linux mcp-config --client codex
```

Review the snippet and add it to your client using the [MCP setup guide](docs/mcp.md). This command prints configuration without changing your settings. Your client launches the stdio MCP server; you give prompts to the client, not to the server.

> Try asking: “Check my Linux machine, open its browser, visit https://example.com, and tell me what you see. Use screenshots before and after you act.”

For an offline walkthrough with synthetic data, try the [project-budget form demo](docs/demo.md). When you're done, run `./bin/agent-linux stop` in terminal B. Closing the viewer alone leaves Linux running; stopping it preserves guest files.

readmeSections.heading: Control the desktop
readmeSections.body:
![Two paths into one local VM: a person uses a viewer and an agent uses MCP. Both can observe the guest, but human ownership pauses agent input.](docs/assets/readme-control.svg)

The viewer and the MCP server connect to the same local Debian VM. Both can observe the desktop. When you take control in the viewer, agent input pauses until you release it.

Run `./bin/agent-linux start` without `--view-only` for interactive control. The CLI chooses the installed native app, Kitty, or the loopback web viewer. If the CLI is on PATH, the bare `agent-linux` command does the same thing in an interactive terminal. You can also choose a viewer explicitly:

| Viewer | Select it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Web** | `start --viewer web` | Private loopback URL; use the on-screen controls to take or release input. See [viewer controls](docs/viewer.md). |
| **Kitty** | `start --viewer kitty` | Live desktop in [Kitty](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/binary/); **F2** hands off input and **Ctrl+]** exits without stopping Linux. |
| **Native Mac preview** | `start --viewer app` | [Build with Xcode/Swift](docs/native-workspace.md) first. Open the searchable [workspace switcher](docs/workspace-switcher.md) with **Command+Shift+K**. |

**Agent workflow:** capture a fresh screenshot → act on the guest → capture again to verify the result. An input acknowledgment is not proof the app changed. Optional [structured browser and UI tools](docs/structured-control.md) require a supporting guest; older guests remain visual-only until upgraded.

readmeSections.heading: Manage workspaces
readmeSections.body:
| I want to… | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Keep work separate | `./bin/agent-linux start --machine work` starts or resumes a [named machine](docs/local-machines.md). Use the same `--machine work` for its MCP configuration and lifecycle commands. |
| See and manage my machines | `./bin/agent-linux machines list --json` lists them; `./bin/agent-linux dashboard --local` opens the [local dashboard](docs/web-console.md). |
| Move a file in or out | Use [`copy-in` and `copy-out`](docs/file-transfer.md) for explicit, bounded file transfers. There is no host project mount or automatic sync. |
| Save or recover a workspace | Stop the machine before creating or restoring a [disk checkpoint](docs/checkpoints.md). Checkpoints capture saved disk state, not RAM or unsaved buffers. |
| Reset, delete, or uninstall | Check the exact machine ID with `status --json`, stop the VM, and review the plan before confirming. See [reset undo/redo and guarded deletion](docs/recoverable-workspaces.md) and [tools uninstall](docs/release.md). Uninstalling tools does not remove VM data. |

The default [managed budget](docs/local-machines.md#managed-resource-budgets) is half the host RAM (including 1 GiB runtime overhead per VM) and two fewer than the host's logical CPU count, with a minimum of one CPU. Agent Linux refuses new starts under macOS memory pressure without stopping running machines.

Local state defaults to `~/.local/share/agent-linux/local`. If you use a custom `--state-dir`, use it consistently for lifecycle, viewers and MCP. Local use has no Agent Linux usage fee; your Mac supplies resources and your agent client/model may charge separately.

readmeSections.heading: Compatibility and limits
readmeSections.body:
| Area | Tested or available | Not established |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Mac host** | M4 Pro, macOS 26.5 (25F71), Lima 2.2.1 with Apple Virtualization | macOS 14+ is a target, not a verified minimum. Intel Mac, Linux and Windows are not local hosts. |
| **Guest** | ARM64 Debian 13 and Xfce 4.20 on one X11 display | No Wayland or guest multi-display. Existing disks retain their provisioned recipe and helper. |
| **Viewers** | Kitty 0.50.0 and Chrome 156 loopback viewing/input on the tested Mac; native app is a local preview | Broader terminal, browser, keyboard and accessibility coverage is pending. |
| **Agents** | Codex CLI and the official Go MCP SDK have local acceptance evidence | Visual tasks require an image-capable client/model. Claude Code and VS Code setup is documented, but their model/tool flows are untested here. |
| **Cloud and billing** | The [cloud prototype](docs/cloud.md) defaults to **SIMULATED**; [billing](docs/billing.md) is sandbox-only | Real-provider and hosted Stripe sandbox acceptance are pending. No live billing or automatic local-to-cloud fallback. |

> **Trust boundary:** Guest commands run inside Linux and can access guest data and the network. NAT can reach host and LAN services; it is not network isolation. Host folders, shared clipboard, host pointer control, SSH-agent forwarding and device sharing are off by default. This is not an independently audited or certified hostile-code sandbox. Screenshots and tool results go to the connected client/model; use disposable guests and synthetic data when trying it out. See [security boundaries](docs/security.md).
